summary: Both tasks are phrased the way the Academic test phrases them: a line graph with four age groups over 30 years for Task 1 and an agree/disagree opinion essay for Task 2. One small wording slip in Task 2 is fixed.
strengths: Task 1 uses the standard rubric ("Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant") and a clear four-line graph with labelled axes.
Task 2 is a typical IELTS work topic with the standard "To what extent do you agree or disagree?" instruction and rubric.

issues.problem: Task 2 read "this change may only benefit workers, not the employers" ("the" is not natural here).
issues.change: Changed to "not employers" in mock1-writing.js. The same sentence is in writing-bank.json (Day 1), which is outside this slice and still has "the employers".

issues.problem: In the graph every age group has exactly the same value in 1998 and 2008, so the last decade is completely flat and gives candidates little to compare.
issues.change: Vary the 2008 values slightly (e.g. 14-24 at 85%, 50 and over at 55%) in writing/day1.svg so there is a final trend to report.
